uu: Refactor line parsing

Re-use archive read's internal buffer instead of creating one within uu
filter. This simplifies memory management.

Prevent situations in which \r\n line endings could be split due to
short reads into \r and \n. This led to uu decoding errors.

Enforce that end marker also ends with a line ending. This is in sync
with uudecode utilities and POSIX standard.

A uu data line longer than a traditional encoded record decodes to at
most 63 bytes. Keep a spare output region of the encoded length for
that line; the reader already requires room for twice the encoded
length.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

uu: Distinguish b64 and uu by code

Introduce ARCHIVE_FILTER_B64 and set reader filter fields based on
detected format. Also support the code when adding write filters.

Resolves #907

Extended uu records no longer share the tail of the output buffer with
the base64 decoder. Give those records their own trailing slot of the
encoded length. The uu loop still reserves twice that length.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

recognize uu/base64 encoded empty files

uuencode:

begin 644 -
`
end

base64:

begin-base64 644 -
====

An extended uu record still occupies its trailing output slot when the
following record is empty.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: Each of the three uu maintenance commits appends one encoded-length spare slot (len bytes, only when len > 128) to the uu output cursor in ST_READ_UU. The filter enters that case only when total + 2*len fits in the 64KiB output buffer, and a uu line decodes to at most 63 bytes, so any single slot stays inside the allocation. The same cursor is advanced by every slot: the refactor commit reserves its slot before the decode loop, the b64/uu split reserves a second slot after the loop, and the empty-file commit reserves a third slot on the success path. Any two of those writes sum to total + 2*len plus the decoded byte count. A line whose length sits on the 2*len ceiling (len == 32767 after a one-byte predecessor) leaves one byte of slack, which the 46 decoded payload bytes overrun, so the second memset writes past the 65536-byte buffer. Deleting any one of the three added blocks leaves the other pair in place, and that pair still overflows on the same input; a single block does not. Traditional uu lines are shorter than 128 bytes and never take the new branch. A correct fix has to account for every reservation against the one 2*len budget — changing only one commit's diff leaves a reachable overflow.
